page: Microsoft Azure FX8-2mds_v2 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the FXmdsv2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor with a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 1 physical core supporting 2 threads (2 vCPUs), 168.0 GB of system memory, and a 472 GB local NVMe SSD. The processor is equipped with a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations.

Benchmark data reveals a significant divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves top-tier single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2344.0 and strong single-threaded compression speeds, such as 34.85 GB/sec in gzip. However, due to the low core count of 1 physical core, multi-core performance is limited, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 2872.0 and stress-ng multi-core performance falling into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is also relatively low at 21.09 GB/sec, though the Passmark memory score remains average.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the FX8-2mds_v2 offers an exceptionally high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 84.0 GB per core, making it a specialized resource density play. It is designed for workloads that require massive memory footprints but minimal parallel CPU processing. This profile is highly suitable for memory-intensive single-threaded applications, small-scale in-memory caching, lightweight database operations, and legacy applications requiring large memory allocations without high multi-threaded compute demands.
description: Microsoft Azure FX8-2mds_v2 is a highly specialized, memory-intensive virtual machine from the FXmdsv2 family. Powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, it provides 1 physical core (2 vCPUs), 168.0 GB of RAM, and 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. While its single-core performance is top-tier, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2344.0 and strong single-threaded compression benchmarks, its multi-core capabilities are constrained by the dual-vCPU limit. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring an extreme memory-to-vCPU ratio of 84.0 GB per core without needing massive parallel processing power. It is best suited for memory-heavy, single-threaded applications, caching layers, and database workloads with low concurrency requirements.
